summary: INV-SOCKET-001 live decisive test COMPLETE. Logged in as owner@cafe103.com (Owner, restaurantId=644). Socket.IO connected to https://presocket.mygenie.online over websocket transport. Client subscribed to own channels: new_order_644, update_table_644, order-engage_644, food_update_644. Ran onAny wire probe for 4 minutes. RESULT: own=0, foreign=6, bytes=1206. Foreign events observed on 'login_disabled_689' and 'login_disabled_523' — RIDs 689 and 523 which are NOT 644. VERDICT: GLOBAL BROADCAST CONFIRMED. Socket.IO server delivers events for OTHER restaurants to an authenticated client, proving the server is NOT room/namespace isolated.

critical.issue: GLOBAL BROADCAST confirmed: authenticated client for restaurantId=644 received 6 events for foreign restaurants 689 and 523 on channel 'login_disabled_<RID>' within 4 minutes. onAny captured them despite client subscribing only to *_644. Server does NOT use rooms/namespaces — every connected client receives ALL restaurants' emissions on the default namespace.

integration_issues.issue: Because server broadcasts globally, frontend RELIES on channel-name-suffix filtering (subscribing only to *_<myRid>) as its sole isolation. Any onAny/wildcard listener leaks foreign-restaurant data. Confirmed live: login_disabled_689 and login_disabled_523 events reached this client's wire.

action_items: SERVER FIX REQUIRED (external Laravel/Socket.IO team): Move per-restaurant emissions to Socket.IO rooms (io.to('restaurant_'+rid).emit) or per-restaurant namespaces. Currently emitting to default namespace globally.
Client hardening (interim): Add defensive suffix check in socketService.on() wrapper to drop payloads whose channel suffix != current restaurantId.
Bandwidth/peak impact: Each POS receives O(N) traffic proportional to total restaurants online — strong candidate root cause for peak-traffic outages. Quantify against observed peak bytes/sec.
critical_code_review_comments: socketService.js exposes window.__SOCKET_SERVICE__ only in NODE_ENV=development — preview build is dev, which enabled the probe. Production build would hide it.
useSocketEvents.js subscribes correctly to *_<restaurantId> — isolation is NAME-based, not ROOM-based. Fragile: any accidental wildcard listener will leak cross-tenant data.
seed_data_creation: None. Passive observation only. NO code changes made per investigation-only mandate.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Decisive evidence gathered. Screenshot of loaded dashboard/loading page saved at .screenshots/03_after_login.png. window.__SOCKET_SERVICE__ was available (dev build). Transport=websocket. socketId=-5GeT4Au_PpQc1T5AAAN. registeredEvents=[new_order_644, update_table_644, order-engage_644, food_update_644] — no duplicates, no foreign in registration (leak is via server broadcast, not client sub). No own-restaurant events during window (quiet on subscribed channels) but foreign login_disabled_* events came through unsolicited.

rca_of_the_issue.evidence: 4-min authenticated observation for RID=644: own=0, foreign=6, bytes=1206. Foreign events on channels login_disabled_689 and login_disabled_523. Client never emitted a join for those channels; server pushed them unsolicited.
rca_of_the_issue.verdict: GLOBAL BROADCAST — foreign>0. Server emits every restaurant's events to every connected client on default namespace. Client-side name-filter is the ONLY thing preventing cross-tenant UI leakage.
rca_of_the_issue.peak_traffic_implication: Each POS receives O(N) traffic where N=total restaurants online — O(N^2) system-wide fanout. Amplifies outage risk on both browsers and socket server.
rca_of_the_issue.mitigation: Server: emit with rooms (io.to('rid_'+rid).emit) or per-restaurant namespaces. Client interim: reject-on-suffix defensive check in socketService.on wrapper.
